claims.content: Customer wants to complete checkout and payment for won auction items by choosing which items to pay for, selecting a shipping method, and finally selecting a payment type.

scope_contract.goal_statement: Customer wants to complete checkout and payment for won auction items by choosing which items to pay for, selecting a shipping method, and finally selecting a payment type.
scope_contract.canonical_success_scenario: The Customer selects the won items to pay for, chooses a shipping method, then selects a payment type, completing checkout and payment for the selected items.
scope_contract.start_boundary: The Customer is at the point of checkout for won auction items and is ready to select which items to pay for.
scope_contract.success_boundary: The Customer has chosen the items, shipping method, and payment type, completing checkout and payment for the selected items.
in_scope_actions: Choosing which won items to pay for
Completing checkout and payment for selected items
variant_dimensions: Which won items the Customer chooses to pay for

claims.content: Customer
The Customer has won at least one auction item and has unpaid auction winnings to pay for.
The Customer has previously chosen either PayPal or Amazon Payments as their default Method of Payment (MOP), which is recorded in the Customer's registration data.

missing_aspects: Explicit evidence that this payment method type must be 'available in the system for checkout' specifically.

Evidence explicitly stating that an account *not* being locked or under review is a precondition for this flow. EC-PC-001 only notes the existence of policies for such states, implying they are exceptions, but does not confirm the positive state required here.

claims.content: The Customer clicks the 'Winnings Alert' link (or the 'Pay now' link in the winner notification email) to begin checkout for won auction items.
The Customer chooses which won items to pay for from a list of won items by checking the 'Pay Now' checkbox next to each item.
The Customer selects a shipping speed option via radio buttons (e.g., USPS Standard or Expedited).
The Customer selects a payment type/checkout option by clicking one of the payment buttons (e.g., 'Check out with PayPal' or 'Check out with Amazon').
Diverges from Step 3: The Customer may select PayPal as the payment method by choosing the corresponding radio button in the 'My Payment Methods' section.

Diverges from Step 3: Instead of using PayPal or Amazon Payments, the Customer may select 'Credit Card' in the 'My New Payment Method' section and enter new billing address details to complete the transaction.
Diverges from Step 3: If the Customer already has a PayPal account, they may log in via the email and password fields on the right side of the page.

Diverges from Step 3: The Customer may create a new PayPal account by selecting 'Create a PayPal account', entering Country (defaulted to United States), and then choosing either 'Bill Me Later®' or 'Credit Card' as the payment method.

Diverges from Step 3: Instead of manually selecting a payment type, returning users with a default Method of Payment (MOP) of PayPal or Amazon Payments are routed to a specific page that offers a choice of shipping methods and initiates the payment process for their winnings.

missing_aspects: Evidence supports the login action but does not explicitly state that this allows the user to 'proceed to pay for the order'.
Evidence supports the account creation steps but does not explicitly confirm that this path leads to completing the specific order ('proceed to pay').

claims.content: At Step 1 (choosing which won items to pay for), if the Customer clicks the 'Checkout Later' button or radio button, the system grays out the page, disables all links, and displays a DIV-layer message that payment can be made within 7 days (168 hours) but unpaid orders will be cancelled after the payment window expires.

missing_aspects: Recovery/return path from the Checkout Later disabled state to resume and complete the same checkout is not documented in the evidence.

Evidence does not explicitly state that the checkout page remains disabled preventing further action; it only describes the immediate UI changes (graying out/disabling links) and the display of the DIV.

claims.content: In the 'Items I've Won' table, the 'Payment Status' column displays 'Paid' for the items whose transaction has been successfully completed.

Upon completing the Amazon or PayPal checkout process, the Customer is returned to a Thank You page that uses the global header and footer and includes a prominent link to the JTVauctions.com home page.

claims.content: Customer wants to complete checkout and payment for won auction items by choosing which items to pay for, selecting a shipping method, and finally selecting a payment type.
The Customer has won at least one auction item and has unpaid auction winnings to pay for.
The Customer has previously chosen either PayPal or Amazon Payments as their default Method of Payment (MOP), which is recorded in the Customer's registration data.
The Customer clicks the 'Winnings Alert' link (or the 'Pay now' link in the winner notification email) to begin checkout for won auction items.
The Customer chooses which won items to pay for from a list of won items by checking the 'Pay Now' checkbox next to each item.
The system offers the Customer a choice of shipping methods.
The Customer selects a shipping speed option via radio buttons (e.g., USPS Standard or Expedited).
The system gets the Customer started on the payment process for their winnings.
The Customer selects a payment type/checkout option by clicking one of the payment buttons (e.g., 'Check out with PayPal' or 'Check out with Amazon').
Diverges from Step 3: The Customer may select PayPal as the payment method by choosing the corresponding radio button in the 'My Payment Methods' section.

Diverges from Step 3: Instead of using PayPal or Amazon Payments, the Customer may select 'Credit Card' in the 'My New Payment Method' section and enter new billing address details to complete the transaction.
Diverges from Step 3: If the Customer already has a PayPal account, they may log in via the email and password fields on the right side of the page.

Diverges from Step 3: The Customer may create a new PayPal account by selecting 'Create a PayPal account', entering Country (defaulted to United States), and then choosing either 'Bill Me Later®' or 'Credit Card' as the payment method.

Diverges from Step 3: Instead of manually selecting a payment type, returning users with a default Method of Payment (MOP) of PayPal or Amazon Payments are routed to a specific page that offers a choice of shipping methods and initiates the payment process for their winnings.

At Step 1 (choosing which won items to pay for), if the Customer clicks the 'Checkout Later' button or radio button, the system grays out the page, disables all links, and displays a DIV-layer message that payment can be made within 7 days (168 hours) but unpaid orders will be cancelled after the payment window expires.
In the 'Items I've Won' table, the 'Payment Status' column displays 'Paid' for the items whose transaction has been successfully completed.

Upon completing the Amazon or PayPal checkout process, the Customer is returned to a Thank You page that uses the global header and footer and includes a prominent link to the JTVauctions.com home page.
